Definition: from G21; exultation; specially, welcome:--gladness, (exceeding) joy.
BiblicalUsage: Agalliasis is exultation — gladness, great joy. The angel promises Zechariah that John's birth will bring joy and gladness; the baby in Elizabeth's womb leaped for joy at Mary's greeting; the first Christians ate their food with gladness and singleness of heart; and the Messiah is anointed with the oil of gladness above His fellows. The word belongs to births, to fellowship, and to the King Himself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word shows joy is not an extra in the Christian life — it is the atmosphere of it. From a baby leaping in the womb to a church breaking bread together, gladness marks the places where God is at work.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; John the Baptist; Mary, Mother of Jesus
